what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Four AI frameworks mapped onto one agent-run newsroom
sections.para: iason's November 2025 paper reads OECD, NIST AI RMF, Japan's guidelines and the EU AI Act side by side and finds five shared principles. Mapping them onto this newsroom and agent team shows the unit should be one agent in one deployment, measured by reach, and that the behaviour policy answers who holds residual risk.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: The frameworks converge, but their unit misfits agents
sections.para: The four frameworks converge on five principles, but each classifies a system before deployment, while an agent's risk is its reach. NIST maps onto policy, gap, footprint and three doors; oversight follows reversibility, since people approve 93% of prompts. Of five principles four run here; risk acceptance is designed.

sections.label: The paper, and what it gets right
sections.line: iason's paper rightly finds five shared principles
sections.para: Sara Martucci and Margherita Ranieri, with Nicola Mazzoni, compare the OECD lens, NIST's process, Japan's division of labour and the Act's tiers. They name five shared principles and warn that treating risk as compliance is strategically shortsighted. Their list of what companies lack ends with reviewing AI outputs, this site's main focus.

sections.label: The unit: a system before deployment, or one agent in one deployment
sections.line: The unit is one agent in one deployment
sections.para: All four instruments classify an AI system before deployment, which suits a model behind a form but not an agent. An agent's risk comes from its connectors, accounts and data. So the unit is the Agent Behaviour Policy: reach, mandate, the gap and its barriers, then the footprint and each row's blast radius.

sections.label: OECD: five dimensions, and the two that matter most for an agent
sections.line: Data and output dimensions matter most for agents
sections.para: People and Planet maps to blast radius, AI Model to a shared model, and Economic Context to the newsroom's small readership. Data and Input becomes the lethal trifecta: private data, untrusted content and a way to send. Task and Output asks the right oversight question on the wrong axis: per system, not output.

sections.label: NIST: govern, map, measure, manage, as they run here
sections.line: Each NIST function maps to a running mechanism here
sections.para: Govern is a written behaviour policy, Map the measured reach, Measure the footprint and hope share, Manage three doors. Rules re-anchor after eighteen summaries a month; one agent's model-only rules fell from 97% to 23%. Oversight is placed by reversibility, since users approve 93% of permission prompts.

sections.label: Japan: three roles, one policy between them
sections.line: Japan's three roles need a policy passing between them
sections.para: Japan splits duties between developer, provider and business user: model vendor, platform and deployer. The guidelines omit what passes between them, which the policy-beside-the-prompt proposal supplies. Microsoft's containers turned three of eight hope rows into boundaries, and the written policy decides liability arguments like Air Canada's.

sections.label: The EU AI Act: the tier, the undefined word, and the dates
sections.line: Accepted is not acceptable, and the Act's dates moved
sections.para: The newsroom is low risk, with proportionality applied per row. Article 9 requires residual risk judged acceptable but never defines it; here acceptance is a named, dated act with three doors. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 moved high-risk dates to 2027 and 2028, so the paper needs a status since.

sections.label: The five principles on one small system
sections.line: Four principles run here; risk registers are designed
sections.para: Ethics runs through a person pressing send; the lifecycle runs with versions and incident write-ups but lacks decommissioning. Human oversight runs by reversibility, and risk tiering runs per row, while the register is designed only. The organisational approach runs at a scale of one person and about fifteen agents.

sections.label: What the graphs add, and the one to build next
sections.line: Next graph: the four frameworks joined as one
sections.para: The Act and NIST already exist as graphs here, including the AI Baseline Control Framework and a ten-layer stack with 119 cited edges. The next graph joins all four frameworks, each its own world, with edges from the texts, plus behaviour policy rows. The first file is a 32-row mapping: twenty-three run, five designed, four argued.

sections.label: Where it is hardest
sections.line: The written mandate is hardest, not ownership or testing
sections.para: Ownership is kept by a register that rolls risks upwards, testing by the second reader, synthetic users and 62 hostile emails, and monitoring is easiest through the footprint. What is hardest, and what no framework asks for in agent-ready form, is the written mandate: without it, every finding is a judgement call.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: A small system, a mapping, not a conformance claim
sections.para: One newsroom, one agent team and one person; the paper targets financial institutions and is quoted, not reproduced. Post-paper dates are this site's, checked on 9 and 13 October 2026. NIST rows are a personal mapping, risk acceptance is a design, the joint graph is proposed, and the 32 rows can be corrected.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Sources: the iason paper and the four frameworks
sections.para: Assembled from my message of 13 October 2026, without a voice memo. Sources are iason's AI Risk Management Frameworks, issue 81, November 2025; the OECD classification framework; the NIST AI RMF and playbook; Japan's AI Guidelines for Business; Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; Anthropic on Claude Code auto mode; and the mapping file.
